Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented enhancement measures based on the recommendations in the consultant’s report, improving areas ranging from energy performance to health-related aspects of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (“HKQAA”) conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2023 environmental data (“2023 Data”). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) for 2023, together with their respective intensities and changes compared with 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level recorded when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data was prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison, except for food waste. The scope of verification covered a total of five office and warehouse premises, comprising four offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and a warehouse located at 5) Riley House in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the five premises. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion with a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the data were tested by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included examining the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was wholly independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2023 Data and concludes that the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable, and that the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Head of Audit, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first year in which the global temperature exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached a new high, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate change mitigation measures. As efforts to tackle global warming continue, climate-related risks will inevitably become more pronounced, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. In addition, heightened geopolitical tensions, increasing fragmentation of the global economy, potentially worsening energy security issues and an uncertain economic outlook are all posing greater challenges to countries’ efforts to address climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Of all regions globally, Asia faces particularly acute transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only an engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the effects of climate change. Asia therefore plays a critical role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions. As Asia’s leading international financial centre, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the region’s transition. To this end, the HKMA announced its “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively embedding sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses both on strengthening the financial sector’s capacity to address climate-related risks and on helping the sector capture the emerging opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work covers four key areas: supporting the banking sector in achieving net zero, investing in a sustainable future, financing net zero, and promoting more inclusive sustainability. The banking system plays a pivotal role in Hong Kong’s and Asia’s net-zero transition, but banks themselves also face considerable risks in the transition process. Under the “Action Agenda”, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier and in their financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance their disclosures of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks’ climate risk management, we also provide guidance on transition planning to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage the associated risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong’s sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing industry transparency in related activities. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to include more sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we hope to channel more capital into sustainability- and transition-related projects. Climate change gives rise to significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. At the same time, however, it also presents the Exchange Fund with opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability impact can be aligned and are not mutually exclusive. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier, and under the “Action Agenda” we have pledged to support Asia’s climate transition through the Exchange Fund’s investments. Sustainable investments currently account for more than 10% of the “Investment Portfolio”. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate Asia’s transition to a low-carbon economy through co-investments. In addition, we published the inaugural “HKMA ESG Expectations” document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Access to finance is particularly important for accelerating the region’s transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances by Asian issuers, including Mainland provincial and municipal governments, Hong Kong plays an important role in directing capital to accelerate the region’s transition. The “Action Agenda” outlines a vision of developing Hong Kong into the region’s preferred sustainable financing platform, as well as the goal of fostering innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstrative effect of the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” to drive green bond innovation—including the issuance of the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year—to expanding the scope of the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” in May last year to cover transition finance instruments, and launching the “Digital Bond Grant Scheme” in November last year, we have remained committed to encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise the funds needed for their decarbonisation transition. A robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosures, and industry professionals equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, under the “Action Agenda” we have pledged to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures and to help bridge the region’s sustainable finance talent and knowledge gaps. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing convenient and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosures among small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the Professional Level module on “Green and Sustainable Finance” under the banking industry’s professional qualifications framework to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged people from different sectors in sustainability discussions, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainability vision. Under the “Action Agenda”, we have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, bringing forward our original commitment by 20 years. In addition, we are actively preparing to comply with international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the Government. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve operational efficiency through digitalisation and foster a culture of sustainability within the organisation, inspiring employees to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic geopolitical shifts have introduced further uncertainty into global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an indisputable fact and is becoming progressively more severe. The current situation leaves no room for complacency in our efforts to address climate change. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong’s financial system while creating opportunities for us in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, spare no effort in advancing sustainability and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we will remain steadfast in our commitment to supporting the building of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the present generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future direction, the timelines for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant initiatives. Through strategic policy development, enhanced supervisory engagement and improvements to internal operations, the HKMA plans to strengthen the capacity of Hong Kong’s financial sector and the HKMA itself to address climate change risks, while promoting Asia’s transition to a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exert influence and contribute to the development of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector’s climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition to net zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - commencing a new round of thematic examinations of banks’ climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation meetings to review banks’ implementation of the HKMA’s relevant supervisory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - finalising the incorporation of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s supervisor-driven stress testing framework; - continuing to advance the incorporation of climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; - commencing preparatory work to formulate relevant supervisory requirements for the local implementation of the climate-related financial risk Pillar 3 disclosure framework to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - completing a new module, GS-2, of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide banks with guidance on transition planning; and - sharing good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech with the industry. In addition to its role as the banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool for identifying green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating the associated flow of capital. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the taxonomy to broaden its coverage, including by incorporating transition elements, adding green economic activities and including climate change adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks’ adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the region’s sustainable financing needs. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, whose expanded scope will cover sustainable projects such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. Despite growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and enterprises, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a wider range of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be used to make existing resources more convenient and accessible; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training needed by the industry. The rapidly evolving sustainable finance market requires the expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA’s key initiatives in 2025 include collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training programmes for the Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners, and identifying areas in which the industry has further training needs through the forthcoming Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030 study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme and review the scope of the scheme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieving net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in support of the broader economic transition. Through a pragmatic and rigorous approach to responsible investment, we will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of its asset portfolios while exploring investment opportunities that can contribute to positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in corporate sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving its net-zero commitment announced in the Action Agenda, the HKMA will continue to advance corporate sustainability at a pragmatic pace by progressively incorporating environmental and social considerations into its strategies, risk assessments and reporting. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. We will also conduct an energy audit and use technological solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government’s Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to applying the principles of energy efficiency and energy conservation when selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, while improving the overall digital experience of our staff, banks and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and working practices. As part of its commitment to good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. The governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability work; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level on the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies; - in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - in respect of other functional areas, relevant committees and working groups, which plan and implement related sustainability initiatives covering banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Cross-Agency Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s different functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of ESG-related strategies, policies and plans in the four functional areas of banking, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, Exchange Fund investments and internal operations; - oversee the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s various functional departments; - assess the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - oversee external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development matters are also invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans relating to their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the Cross-Agency Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Cross-Agency Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Cross-Agency Steering Group’s work, refer to the chapter “Enhancing the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are affected by various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risks and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a sustainable finance hub in the region and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Agenda comprises eight goals in four areas. To help the industry achieve the goals relating to banking policy, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks strive to achieve net zero in their own operations by 2030 and net zero financed emissions by 2050. All banks increase transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2, “Transition Planning”. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capabilities to address the net-zero transition and manage the associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors set out by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (“Basel Committee”) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risks. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (“ISSB Standards”) and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Agenda. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (“Taxonomy”) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help channel capital towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors and is designed to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy and the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating elements relevant to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to broaden the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate green and sustainable financing. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and continued to support banks in building their capabilities to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into the banking supervisory process. To help banks strengthen their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic examinations and consultation meetings, mainly including: - establishing a robust governance structure that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board and senior management - ensuring effective oversight of key areas relating to climate-related risks: (1) facilitating and overseeing the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced and Responsive Supervision Roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a range of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA commenced a round of thematic examinations of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”. The thematic examinations covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, controls and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA conducted a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new group of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”, and to understand the challenges they faced. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to individual banks’ circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that, under various scenarios, including one assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn, Hong Kong’s banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience to severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the exercise was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognises the numerous data- and methodology-related challenges banks face in managing climate risks and has therefore been pursuing various initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA has been collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published a practical application guide and two Regtech Adoption Practice Guides (in English), describing technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also organised the third “FiNETech”, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore collaboration in green fintech. Recognising that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and supervisors to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS released the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Plans Working Group, the HKMA participated in analysing the interactions between the transition plans of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Practical Guidance on Banks’ Adoption of Greentech” (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects examining the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of firms’ environmental performance in mitigating monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition towards a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only enhanced our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, supporting the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, the research supports the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandum series. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the HKIMR’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this participation, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, while drawing insights from these discussions to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial market, enhancing sustainability disclosures by the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures Bridging the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to more than 110 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including their currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the Programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects, and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (“Sustainable Bond Programme”). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes a Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency offering comprised bonds of different tenors denominated in renminbi, US dollars and euros. The bonds attracted strong demand from a diverse range of investors, with subscriptions exceeding US$15 billion equivalent. The 20- and 30-year renminbi green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and were its longest-tenor renminbi bonds to date, providing new benchmarks for the market and further demonstrating the role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further broadened the range of offshore renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond offerings reflects investors’ recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As at end-2024, grants had been approved under the Scheme for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. In May 2024, the Scheme was extended for three years to 2027, and its scope of subsidies was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong’s transition finance platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions. - Grants approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion (as at end-2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope of subsidies expanded to transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, with encouraging results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, including RMB2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds and RMB900 million of social bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion of blue bonds and RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds. These bond issuances once again highlighted Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through the above measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained Asia’s largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in 2024, with bonds arranged in Hong Kong totalling US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world’s first tokenised government green bond and the world’s first multi-currency digital bond, respectively. These issuances demonstrated the Government’s support for regional market participants in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in green and sustainable finance. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (“Steering Group”) has been working towards the adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (“ISSB Standards”) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (“Questionnaire”), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises (“SMEs”). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable businesses to complete it online (see the QR code below). Based on industry feedback and the latest international developments, the HKMA is refining the Questionnaire to make it more user-friendly, including by identifying its core questions and providing common use cases. We are also seeking to improve the Questionnaire’s compatibility with other supporting tools on the Steering Group’s website. For more information about the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, demonstrating its commitment. The Report contains extensive information on the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks, as well as its plans and implementation progress towards achieving its climate goals. For details of sustainability disclosures concerning our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA”. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local banking practitioners’ knowledge and skills in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (“HKIB”) launched the foundation level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in July 2023. The module is designed to help banking professionals acquire knowledge of green and sustainable finance and develop relevant professional competencies more effectively, covering four key areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance and controls. In addition, the professional level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, aimed at middle- and senior-level banking practitioners responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide banking practitioners with the necessary training, the HKIB, as the administrator of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, launched a foundation-level training programme for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop a professional-level training programme. To understand the banking sector’s further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry on the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030” study, with the results targeted for publication in 2025. This joint study follows up on the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it formulate and adjust talent development strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students undertaking sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, 85 international and local programmes had been registered as eligible training programmes under the Scheme, and more than 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (“CASI”), the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office and CASI jointly organised a two-day training workshop in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (“GFANZ”) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritises sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of “capital preservation first, long-term growth thereafter”, believing that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate associated investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We incorporate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner and continue to explore various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA issued the “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to foster a future in which finance and sustainable development advance in tandem. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while taking into account the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the EFIO’s Sustainable Investment Team. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and oversees the EFIO’s ESG initiatives. Proposals and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across the HKMA’s different functions, including the EFIO, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different EFIO teams on ESG integration and assists the EFIO’s senior management in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across various investment programmes: - Public market investments — The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior EFIO staff, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed-income portfolios through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (for details, see “Promoting Active Ownership” under the “Risk Management” section on page 39). - Private market investments — The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, may affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The United Nations Environment Programme’s Emissions Gap Report 2024 projects that the global average temperature will rise by 2.6°C to 3.1°C above pre-industrial levels unless greenhouse gas emissions are rapidly reduced through large-scale global mobilisation. Uncertainty surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, resulting in greater market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also expose investments to additional risks of physical damage and financial loss. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related considerations in ESG integration. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and continues to make progress towards this target through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the “Action Agenda”, which reinforces the Exchange Fund’s commitments and efforts relating to the climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from investible opportunities. Investing in a sustainable future Achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier - Actively broaden the scope and range of sustainable investments, particularly climate-transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition outlook considerations - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to follow them - Aim to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 or earlier Supporting the region’s transition through investment - Continue engaging with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that facilitate the transition - Continue identifying and prioritising quality investment opportunities that can facilitate Asia’s transition and generate positive global impact First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investible universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and equipped with superior technologies and sound corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, tackling climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Simply excluding or divesting from the relevant investments will not resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and the exercise of active ownership, encouraging them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices and thereby bringing about positive change for both the industries themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, in order to drive economy-wide decarbonisation. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of its portfolio depends not only on adjustments within the portfolio itself, but also on broad-based economic transition. While there is no perfect single solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategy in 2024 by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive the transition while supporting the net-zero goals of both the Exchange Fund and the world. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including ESG integration and stewardship in fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting various types of assets aligned with pathways towards net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or providers of climate solutions, complemented by stewardship to facilitate corporate transition. In private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on investments that facilitate the transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate the climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio”, with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments — The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the use of a customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the related case studies in “Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds”). - Private market investments — The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio and capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and assesses investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see examples in “Joining Forces to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond”). - Passive portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios whose investment benchmarks are not ESG indices - Actively managed governance-themed portfolios - Actively managed ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable attributes, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around the energy transition and decarbonisation globally, in Asia and in the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The “MCPP One Planet” programme, which provides Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental institution. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including the upgrading of ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades covered enhancements to monitoring and control systems and pump performance, generating positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling. In addition to the ongoing treatment of wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. The facilities also use gas generated during sludge treatment to fuel boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond finances multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a country’s canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river flows to arid regions. The project’s primary objective is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA’s key priorities in 2024 in delivering on this commitment was its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target and in alignment with the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda”. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to fostering staff training and well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance the public’s financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee endorsed in October 2024 the HKMA’s new target of achieving net zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030 or earlier as part of the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) provides guidance on implementing sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. An Office Green Group and a Volunteer Services Group, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ways to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: the environment, its people and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonising and digitalising the HKMA’s daily operations, with the goal of achieving net zero emissions by 2030 or earlier - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with Government guidelines - Promote greener operational practices across the financial sector and the wider community - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens employees’ sense of belonging - Provide a high-quality work environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Foster a caring culture towards the community - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives The HKMA is mindful of climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the “Action Agenda”. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition to net zero, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impacts of its daily operations by reducing carbon emissions, saving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for power generation by local electricity companies. In addition, the HKMA has established a digital workplace to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. The HKMA also recognises the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainability-friendly practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under its primary target of achieving net zero emissions by 2030, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procure with as low a carbon footprint as practicable. In this regard, since 2023 the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offsetting schemes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market’s low-carbon transition through initiatives ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter describes in detail the HKMA’s strategies for environmental leadership, promoting staff well-being and caring for the community. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To assess more effectively the potential operational impacts of climate change, the HKMA identifies various climate-related risks and reviews their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring operational continuity, the HKMA’s offices incorporate various measures into their design to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions and waste generated by its operations, as well as its energy and paper consumption. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its corporate operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated using fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA takes a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods, including capital goods, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example by upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 with a view to achieving fully green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres. As part of a data centre facilities upgrade project in 2024, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design enables flexible capacity expansion, enhances operating efficiency under partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technology and higher power density, thereby helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers’ software update cycles, thereby prolonging the period during which the devices can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to support the formulation of targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are provided at convenient locations throughout the HKMA’s offices. To increase the recycling rate, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Pledge Scheme for Large-scale Events”, pledging to take measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to give priority to procuring goods that meet the environmental specifications in the Government’s “Green Procurement List”, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as by combining multiple trips wherever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard-certified carbon offsetting schemes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these schemes focus on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the end of May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. This provided an excellent opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment and drive to put environmental sustainability into practice in its internal operations. The programme included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “kokedama”, an indoor plant arrangement originating in Japan. Waste audit results were also shared, and an operator of a community recycling centre introduced recycling best practices. To sustain the momentum of “Green Month”, the HKMA launched a recycling campaign lasting approximately six months in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that the collective impact of small changes in individual habits could significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the “Go Green, Recycle Clean” video, in which several senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders encouraging staff to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to assess employees’ awareness of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help shape future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA regards itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to leading and accelerating the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable operational practices across the financial sector and the wider community. The HKMA introduced various measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform’s coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, facilitating their submission of certain regulatory information. The expansion aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 included SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a streamlined submission process, and the Intelligent Information and Document Management System, which provides users with a centralised platform featuring advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the “Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, and their respective intensities for 2024. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, as well as their corresponding intensities, for 2023 and 2024. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the “GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of six office and warehouse premises, comprising five offices located at (1) Two International Finance Centre, (2) Hopewell Centre, (3) One Pacific Place, (4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and (5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at (6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed selected representative Data and supporting evidence from the six premises. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the Data were tested by tracing selected sample data to their sources, while the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for collecting and reporting the Data. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. HKQAA’s verification team was not involved in the preparation of the Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance regarding the Data and concludes that: - the Data are materially accurate and reliable; - the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Head of Audit, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
